what: The budget-ranking backtest (allocation.py). Higher share is better.

interval.caveat: Percentile interval from 18 resampled years (block 1). With this few years it is too narrow: in simulation a nominal 95% interval covered the truth about 88% of the time with 8 years and 92% with 18 (80% and 90% with two-year blocks), and is expected to be less if years are dependent. These coverage figures come from a simulation with independent years and a true difference of zero, not from this project's data.

model_minus_better_rule.note: The better rule was picked AFTER seeing both rules' results on these same years. That makes this comparison harder for the model than a comparison with one rule named in advance, and it makes a 'clear loss' look more certain than it is. In a review simulation (400 repetitions, k = 15, 18 years, three rankings with no skill; not this project's data) a no-skill model was called a clear loss against the better of two no-skill rules about 7.7% of the time, against a nominal 2.5%, and a clear win about 1.3% of the time. The comparisons with rule A and with rule B, each named in advance, are reported beside this one.
